name: devbridge-mcp

tools.name: read_page
tools.description: Get an accessibility tree representation of elements on the page. Returns element references (ref_1, ref_2, etc.) that can be used with other tools.

tabId.description: Tab ID. Get available IDs from tabs_context.

filter.description: Filter: "interactive" for buttons/links/inputs only, "all" for everything. Default: "all"

ref_id.description: Focus on a specific element by ref ID

tools.name: javascript_exec
tools.description: Execute JavaScript code in the context of the current page. Returns the result of the last expression — simple expressions work directly (e.g. `document.title` → "Example Page"; `1 + 1` → 2; `{ a: 1, b: 2 }` → the object). Do NOT use top-level `return` statements. For multi-statement logic, wrap in an IIFE: `(() => { const x = 1; return x; })()`. Functions and non-serializable values fall back to their string description. Output is sanitized for secrets and truncated to ~50KB.

text.description: JavaScript code to execute in the page context. The result of the last expression is returned. Do NOT use 'return' statements.

tabId.description: Tab ID. Get available IDs from tabs_context.

frameId.description: Target frame ID (omit or 0 for the main frame; positive integer for a sub-frame from read_page, e.g. 2 from `f2::ref_5`). Evaluating inside a cross-origin frame is supported and has no extra permission cost at runtime, but the code executes in the target frame's MAIN world — avoid relying on main-frame globals like `window.React` unless you know the frame also has them.

tools.name: read_console
tools.description: Read console messages from the page. Supports pattern filtering, error-only mode, and clearing. Auto-cleared on top-level navigation to a different hostname. Storage holds up to 10000 messages per tab (older messages are dropped).

tabId.description: Tab ID. Get available IDs from tabs_context.

onlyErrors.description: Only return error messages. Default: false

clear.description: Clear messages after reading. Default: false

tools.name: read_network
tools.description:
**Tracking activates on the first call to this tool for a given tab** — requests fired before that first call are NOT retroactively captured. Call once at the start of any flow you want to inspect (e.g. before navigate / form_input), then call again later to read the buffer. Once activated, tracking persists across reloads/navigations until the tab closes — check trackingStartedAt in the response to know the coverage window. Reads network requests from the page using CDP (XHR, Fetch, etc.). Includes cross-origin requests. Auto-cleared on top-level navigation to a different hostname. Storage holds up to 1000 entries per tab (older entries are dropped). 

**Two modes (mutually exclusive):**
- **Bulk mode** (no requestId): returns a request list. Pass `includeBody: true` to attach response bodies (default 10KB truncation per entry via bodyMaxBytes). Only XHR/Fetch/Document bodies are fetched by default. If total payload exceeds the ~1MB browser→host channel limit, the response is hard-truncated with an error message guiding you to use detail mode.
- **Detail mode** (pass requestId): fetches the full body for a single request. Supports chunked retrieval via bodyOffset + bodyLength for large responses. Single chunk soft cap ~900KB; cumulative cap 10MB (bodies larger than 10MB should be fetched via javascript_exec instead). Returns responseBody (string or null), responseBodyTruncated, nextBodyOffset (null when complete), and responseBodySize. Non-binary responses are JSON.parse-attempted when fully returned in one chunk.

**Error codes:** F1 body released by Chrome — retry immediately or use javascript_exec fetch. F2 body >10MB — use javascript_exec. F3 bulk payload budget exceeded — switch to detail mode per requestId. F4 cross-origin iframe (OOPIF) body — use javascript_exec with frameId.

tabId.description: Tab ID. Get available IDs from tabs_context.

urlPattern.description: URL substring to filter requests (bulk mode only; mutually exclusive with requestId)

limit.description: Max requests to return. Default: 100 (bulk mode only; mutually exclusive with requestId)

clear.description: Clear requests after reading. Default: false (bulk mode only; mutually exclusive with requestId)

includeBody.description: Include response body for each request in bulk mode. Bodies are truncated to bodyMaxBytes (default 10KB). Only XHR/Fetch/Document types are fetched by default; binary (base64) bodies are returned as-is. Mutually exclusive with requestId.

bodyMaxBytes.description: Max bytes per response body in bulk includeBody mode. Default: 10240 (10KB). Mutually exclusive with requestId.

bodyResourceTypes.description: Resource types to fetch body for in bulk mode. Default: ["XHR", "Fetch", "Document"]. Mutually exclusive with requestId.

requestId.description: Target a single request by its CDP requestId for detail mode. Returns full response body (up to ~900KB per chunk, 10MB cumulative cap). Mutually exclusive with urlPattern / limit / clear / includeBody / bodyMaxBytes.

bodyOffset.description: Byte offset for chunked body retrieval in detail mode (default: 0). Use nextBodyOffset from the previous response to iterate through large bodies.

bodyLength.description: Max bytes to return in detail mode per call (default: ~900KB soft cap). Use with bodyOffset for chunked retrieval of large bodies.

tools.name: computer
tools.description: Perform browser actions. Uses CDP for precise input simulation. Action groups: (1) page interaction — left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, type, screenshot, wait, scroll, key, left_click_drag, zoom (crops region=[x0,y0,x1,y1], returns 2× JPEG), scroll_to, hover. Operates on DOM elements via ref/selector/coordinate. (2) canvas_* family — canvas_screenshot, canvas_click, canvas_drag, canvas_draw_path, canvas_gesture, canvas_scroll, canvas_hover, canvas_keypress, canvas_pixel, canvas_pixel_bulk, canvas_hit_test, canvas_record. Operates on `<canvas>` internals via canvasX/canvasY (bitmap pixels by default; set coordinateSpace="css" for CSS pixels) plus dedicated params (pointerType, pressure, gestureKind, points, ...). Use these for chart/game/whiteboard canvases when DOM refs are insufficient. Keyboard: `key` accepts named keys, single characters, punctuation, and chords with modifiers — e.g. "Enter", "ctrl+/", "ctrl+-", "meta+a", "shift+Tab", "ctrl+shift+["; modifier aliases option/opt→alt and super/win/windows→meta are accepted, unrecognized modifiers raise an error. `type` inserts text directly and bypasses the IME (CJK is committed literally, not intercepted); pass `submit:true` to press a real Enter after inserting (for search boxes / React inputs that enable their submit button or autocomplete only on a key event) — omit it and behavior is insert-only as before. `left_click_drag` accepts `modifiers` (e.g. "shift") held for the entire drag (press→move→release), for shift-select / modifier-drag; and `path` ([[x1,y1],...]) for intermediate waypoints — use when a straight line would trigger unintended reorders (e.g. cross-container SortableJS: path=[[exitX,targetY]], end=[targetX,targetY] where targetY is the desired insertion row in the target list — the cursor y when entering the target container determines the drop position, not just the release point). Page-interaction target resolution (priority order): `ref` (preferred when `read_page` has been called): DOM-truth, supports closed shadow. `selector` (preferred when user provides a CSS selector explicitly, e.g. "#submit"): saves a `read_page` roundtrip; supports open shadow piercing; main frame by default — use `frameId` for sub-frames. `coordinate` (fallback for image regions / pixel-level targets on non-canvas content; for `<canvas>` content use the canvas_* family instead).

tabId.description: Tab ID. Get available IDs from tabs_context.

text.description: Text to type or key(s) to press

ref.description: Element ref from read_page (preferred over coordinate for clickable targets). REQUIRED for all canvas_* actions — they only accept ref (the canvas element), not selector/coordinate.

selector.description: CSS selector targeting a single element (alternative to ref/coordinate). Supports open shadow piercing; main frame by default — use frameId for sub-frames. Strict mode: multi-match requires selectorIndex. Closed shadow elements require ref instead. Max 1024 chars.

selectorIndex.description: Disambiguator (0-indexed) when selector matches multiple elements. Out-of-range raises a [selector] error (no silent clamp).

start_selector.description: CSS selector for left_click_drag start point (paired with selector or coordinate as end). Same constraints as selector.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys held during the action: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (aliases: "control", "command", "meta", "option"/"opt"→alt, "super"/"win"/"windows"→meta), combinable with "+" (e.g. "shift+alt"). Applies to click actions (left_click/right_click/double_click/triple_click) and to left_click_drag (held for the entire drag). An unrecognized modifier raises an error.

submit.description: For action "type" only: when true, dispatch a real Enter keydown/keyup after inserting the text (to trigger search buttons / autocomplete that listen for key events). Defaults to false; when omitted the behavior is identical to today (insertText only, no key event).

path.description: Optional intermediate waypoints for left_click_drag, as [[x1,y1],[x2,y2],...]. The drag moves: mousePressed @ start → through each waypoint → mouseReleased @ end. Use when a direct line would unintentionally trigger elements along the route (e.g. cross-container SortableJS drag: exit the source container horizontally before moving to the target). IMPORTANT for insertion accuracy: most drag libraries (SortableJS, react-dnd) determine the drop position from where the cursor is when it enters the target container — not just the final release point. To control exactly where the item is inserted, set the waypoint y (and the end coordinate y) to the desired insertion position in the target list, not the source element y. Example: dragging from source list item at (200,300) to insert above item at (700,450) in target list → path=[[500,450]], coordinate=[700,450]. This ensures the cursor enters the target container at y=450, placing the item there.

frameId.description: Target frame ID for selector resolve (omit or 0 for the main frame; positive integer for a sub-frame from read_page, e.g. 2 from "f2::ref_5"). When frameId > 0, the resolved coordinate is accumulated to top-level viewport via the iframe ancestor chain. Has no effect on ref / coordinate paths (ref carries its own frame prefix; coordinate is always top-level).

region.description: [x0,y0,x1,y1] viewport CSS coordinates for zoom; crops this region and returns a 2× scaled JPEG screenshot

repeat.description: Key repeat count (applies to both action "key" and action "canvas_keypress")

downscale.description: canvas_screenshot: downscale large canvases to ≤2MP. Default true

maxPx.description: canvas_screenshot: explicit pixel cap, clamped to [100000, 8000000]

canvasX.description: canvas_click/drag/draw_path/hover/scroll/pixel: bitmap-pixel X inside canvas. Used with canvas_* actions.

canvasY.description: canvas_click/drag/draw_path/hover/scroll/pixel: bitmap-pixel Y inside canvas. Used with canvas_* actions.

canvasNormalizedX.description: canvas_click/hover: 0..1 normalized X (alternative to canvasX). LLM rough visual targeting.

coordinateSpace.description: canvas_*: coordinate space. "bitmap" (default) = canvas.width/height pixels, "css" = CSS pixels

steps.description: canvas_drag: number of mouseMoved interpolation steps (default 10, clamped [2,100])

points.description: canvas_draw_path: ordered [[x,y],...] points, max 500. canvas_pixel_bulk: max 1000.

pressureCurve.description: canvas_draw_path: per-point pressure curve (parallel to points)

gestureKind.description: canvas_gesture: type of gesture. (Backwards-compatible alias `kind` also accepted in service-worker.)

pinchScale.description: canvas_gesture pinch: scale ratio. >1 spread, <1 pinch

swipeDirection.description: canvas_gesture swipe: convenience direction (alternative to dx/dy)

keys.description: canvas_keypress: keys to press, space-separated chords (e.g. "v" or "ctrl+z" or "Escape").

restoreFocus.description: canvas_keypress: restore canvas tabIndex to original after press (default true)

imageDataWidth.description: canvas_pixel: explicit raw imageData width override (advanced)

imageDataHeight.description: canvas_pixel: explicit raw imageData height override (advanced)

library.description: canvas_hit_test: which adapter to use ("auto" = first detected). Default "auto"

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Take a screenshot of the current page. Returns the image plus an imageId that can be passed to upload_image.

tabId.description: Tab ID. Get available IDs from tabs_context.

tools.name: navigate
tools.description: Navigate to a URL or use "back"/"forward" for history navigation.

url.description: URL to navigate to. Use "forward" or "back" for history navigation. Only http(s) URLs are allowed; non-http(s) protocols (file://, javascript:, data:, about:, ftp:, ...) will be rejected.

tabId.description: Tab ID. Get available IDs from tabs_context.

force.description: If the page shows a "Leave site?" dialog because of unsaved changes, discard those changes and navigate anyway. Defaults to false.

tools.name: get_page_text
tools.description: Extract the text content of the page as plain text (no HTML), prioritizing article/main content.

tabId.description: Tab ID. Get available IDs from tabs_context.

tools.name: find
tools.description: Search for elements on the page by text content, aria-label, placeholder, or role (with keyword synonym expansion). Returns up to 20 matching element refs. Broad keywords may also match ancestor containers (e.g. <body>) whose text contains the query — when several refs come back, confirm the interactive one with read_page before acting.

query.description: Text to search for in page elements (searches text content, aria-label, placeholder, role)

tabId.description: Tab ID. Get available IDs from tabs_context.

tools.name: form_input
tools.description: Set the value of a form element (input, textarea, select, checkbox, contenteditable) by ref. For rich text editors with their own data model (Notion, Slate, ProseMirror, Lexical), prefer `computer.click` + `computer.type` instead — `form_input` only sets the DOM directly, which the editor may revert on its next render.

ref.description: Element ref from read_page or find

value.description: Value to set. String for text inputs, boolean for checkboxes, number for numeric inputs.

tabId.description: Tab ID. Get available IDs from tabs_context.

tools.name: resize_window
tools.description: Resize the browser window containing the specified tab. Resizing after a screenshot may invalidate coordinates captured earlier — re-screenshot before using coordinate-based actions.

tabId.description: Tab ID. Get available IDs from tabs_context.

tools.name: tabs_close
tools.description: Close a tab by tab ID. If the tab is not closeable in the current workspace the call returns an error — read the error message for the reason.

tabId.description: Tab ID. Get available IDs from tabs_context.

tools.name: tabs_create
tools.description: Open a new tab in the current workspace.

sessionId.description: MCP session ID. Defaults to 'default'. Tab will be added to this session's tab group.

tools.name: upload_image
tools.description: Upload a previously captured screenshot (by imageId, as returned by the screenshot tool) to a file input element on the page.

imageId.description: ID of a previously captured screenshot

tabId.description: Tab ID. Get available IDs from tabs_context.

filename.description: Filename for the uploaded image. Default: image.png

tools.name: gif_creator
tools.description: Record browser actions as an animated GIF. Start recording, perform actions, then export. Frame buffer is a rolling window — at most the most recent 120 frames are retained; long or high-FPS recordings simply drop older frames (no error is raised). Export runs gif.js in an offscreen document with a 60-second encoding timeout; if export times out, segment long sessions: stop_recording → export sooner, then start_recording again for the next segment.

tabId.description: Tab ID. Get available IDs from tabs_context.

download.description: Whether to trigger a browser download

showClickIndicators.description: Overlay click ripples on captured frames. Default: true

showDragPaths.description: Draw drag trajectories as overlays. Default: true

showActionLabels.description: Render textual action labels on each frame. Default: true

showProgressBar.description: Render a progress bar across the bottom of each frame. Default: false

showWatermark.description: Stamp a corner watermark on each frame. Default: false

quality.description: GIF encoding quality. Lower is better; typical 1-30. Default: 10

tools.name: tabs_context
tools.description: List the tabs available in the current workspace, including their IDs for use with other tools. Set createIfEmpty=true to open a new window with a blank tab if no tabs are available. Each tab includes debuggerAttached (devbridge|other|none|unknown): 'other' means another extension or DevTools holds the debugger — tab-level CDP tools (cdp_command/read_network/cdp_subscribe) will fail there; disable the conflicting extension (look it up by debuggerAttachedBy id at chrome://extensions) or pick a 'none'/'devbridge' tab. An 'other' tab may also carry maybeSelfStale: true — a heuristic hint that this is most likely DevBridge's own zombie session left over after a service-worker restart (not a real conflict). Just issue a tab-level CDP call: it usually recovers the session transparently with no user action needed; if it instead errors, the tab really is held by another extension.

createIfEmpty.description: If no tabs are available in the workspace, open a new window with a blank tab. Default: false.

tools.name: file_upload
tools.description: Upload local filesystem files to a file input element on the page using CDP DOM.setFileInputFiles.

paths.description: Absolute paths to files to upload. Can be single or multiple files.

ref.description: Element reference ID of the file input (e.g., "ref_1").

tabId.description: Tab ID. Get available IDs from tabs_context.

tools.name: reset_session
tools.description: Reset MCP session boundary: clear per-turn permission grants (turnApprovedDomains), hide all visual indicators, drain in-flight requests (≤5s) + 50ms IPC flush buffer, then reconnect the native host. Call when starting a new AI debugging session or when permission/indicator state may be stale.

tools.name: cdp_command
tools.description: Execute any CDP method (escape hatch); prefer dedicated tools first. _help lists domains; {domain:'X'} methods; {method:'X.y'} returns the full parameter signature (name, type, optional) + docUrl — no external doc fetch needed. Names are PascalCase.camelCase; tabId required. ⚠️ Browser.*/Target.* are NOT callable via the tab debugger; use extension_call or pass cdpSessionId from Target.attachToBrowserTarget. Fetch.*/Debugger.enable are sticky. If a call reports 'attached by another extension', a debugger-using extension (DevTools / Recorder / another AI assistant) holds the tab — disable it, then reset_session.

method.description: CDP method name in camelCase (e.g. "Fetch.enable", "Network.getCookies"). Pass "_help" with no other args to list domains; "_help" with `{ domain }` lists methods; "_help" with `{ method }` returns the full parameter signature (name, type, optional) plus docUrl — no need to fetch external docs. CDP names are camelCase — "Fetch.Enable" is wrong. Note: "Target.getTargets" is a special case — it does not require tabId and will be handled directly via chrome.debugger.getTargets().

params.description: Parameters object for the CDP method (passes through verbatim).

tabId.description: Tab ID. Get available IDs from tabs_context.

cdpSessionId.description: Optional CDP session ID for OOPIF / sub-target routing (from Target.attachToBrowserTarget etc.). Omit for the main target. Distinct from the internal routing sessionId.

timeoutMs.description: Per-call timeout in ms (max 30000). On timeout the debugger is automatically detached and an error is thrown — re-issue the command after re-attaching.

tools.name: cdp_subscribe
tools.description: ⚠️ For AI-automated flows, prefer cdp_events_read (always-on ring buffer). Subscribe to CDP events for N ms (max 25000). tabId is REQUIRED (from tabs_context). Suits Fetch.requestPaused / Debugger.paused / dialog flows. Two-step (MUST be separate, non-parallel tool calls): (1) cdp_subscribe FIRST to arm it; (2) in a LATER call trigger the action. This call BLOCKS until its window closes, so a trigger issued in the same call/batch only runs after capture has ended and is always missed — for AI-driven triggers, use cdp_events_read. Pass `until` for early-exit. Returns { events, durationMs }.

event.description: CDP event name (e.g. "Fetch.requestPaused", "Page.javascriptDialogOpening"). The matching domain must be enabled (e.g. call cdp_command('Fetch.enable', ...) first). ⚠️ Pre-arm before triggering: subscribe first, then perform the action that produces the event.

durationMs.description: Subscription window in ms (max 25000 to stay under SW 30s idle reclaim).

tabId.description: Tab ID. Get available IDs from tabs_context.

cdpSessionId.description: Optional CDP session ID for OOPIF / sub-target filtering (from Target.attachToBrowserTarget etc.). Omit for the main target. Distinct from the internal routing sessionId.

firstMatch.description: Return as soon as any event arrives.

matchArgs.description: Subset deep-match against the first listener arg / CDP params (lodash _.isMatch semantics). Example: { state: { current: "complete" } } matches { id, state: { current: "complete", ... } }. Example 2 (chrome.tabs.onUpdated): { status: "complete" } matches when changeInfo arg has status===complete. Does not support predicate functions / regex / wildcards in v1.

count.description: Return after collecting N matching events. Default: 1.

matchEvent.description: Return when an event with this CDP method name fires (use with multi-event subscriptions).

until.description: Optional early-exit predicate; subscription resolves immediately on match instead of waiting for durationMs.

tools.name: extension_call
tools.description: Call chrome.<namespace>.<method>(...args) via structured RPC (escape hatch). Path format: 'storage.local.get'. extension_call('_help') lists allowed namespaces + method/event names with full parameter signatures (name, type, optional) + docUrl — no external doc fetch needed. Blocked (v1): debugger (use cdp_command), enterprise, identity, management, nativeMessaging. Args is an array of method params; returns the result. Void methods → { success: true, void: true }.

method.description: Path "<namespace>.<method>" (omit `chrome.` prefix), e.g. "storage.local.get", "cookies.getAll". Pass "_help" with no args to list allowed namespaces; "_help" with `{ namespace }` lists methods/events.

args.description: Positional arguments passed verbatim to the chrome.* method. Default: [].

tools.name: extension_subscribe
tools.description: ⚠️ MUST be a separate, non-parallel call placed BEFORE the trigger — this call BLOCKS until its window closes, so a same-turn/parallel trigger only runs after capture has ended and is always missed; for AI-automated flows use extension_events_read instead. Subscribe to chrome.<namespace>.<event>.addListener for N ms (max 25000). Path format: 'tabs.onUpdated'. Same namespace whitelist as extension_call. Pass `until` for early-exit; optional tabFilter keeps only events whose first arg matches a tabId. Returns { events:[{ args, timestamp }], durationMs, truncated? }.

event.description: ⚠️ Subscribe BEFORE triggering the event — chrome.* events do not replay. Path "<namespace>.<event>" (omit `chrome.` prefix), e.g. "downloads.onChanged", "tabs.onUpdated". Same namespace whitelist as extension_call.

durationMs.description: Subscription window in ms (max 25000 to stay under SW 30s idle reclaim).

tabFilter.description: Optional tabId filter. Events whose first listener arg equals tabFilter are kept; others are dropped early. Useful for chrome.tabs.* events that take (tabId, ...) signatures.

firstMatch.description: Return as soon as any event arrives.

matchArgs.description: Subset deep-match against the first listener arg / CDP params (lodash _.isMatch semantics). Example: { state: { current: "complete" } } matches { id, state: { current: "complete", ... } }. Example 2 (chrome.tabs.onUpdated): { status: "complete" } matches when changeInfo arg has status===complete. Does not support predicate functions / regex / wildcards in v1.

count.description: Return after collecting N matching events. Default: 1.

until.description: Optional early-exit predicate; subscription resolves immediately on match instead of waiting for durationMs.

tools.name: cdp_events_read
tools.description: Read CDP events from the always-on ring buffer (per-tab, per-method, 500 events/method). No subscribe step needed — events are captured once the DevBridge debugger is attached to the tab. If another extension holds the debugger (or it was never attached), the buffer is empty; call screenshot or any attaching tool first to ensure attachment. Use `since` cursor for incremental reads: first call returns nextSince, next call passes it as since. Returns { events:[{ method, params, timestamp }], nextSince, truncated?, droppedCount? }. Caveat: cross-document navigation auto-detaches the debugger and clears this buffer — use cdp_subscribe for navigate-triggered events. For user-initiated browser actions (dialogs, downloads) where you need to react while the action is pending, cdp_subscribe is still appropriate.

tabId.description: Tab ID. Get available IDs from tabs_context.

event.description: CDP method name filter, e.g. 'Page.loadEventFired'. Omit to return all methods.

since.description: Timestamp cursor (ms). Return only events with timestamp > since. Omit to return all buffered events.

limit.description: Max events to return. Default: 200, max: 500.

clear.description: Clear matched entries from buffer after reading. Default: false.

tools.name: extension_events_read
tools.description: ⚠️ CALL THIS ONCE BEFORE triggering any action you want to monitor — the listener is LAZILY registered on first read, so events before the first call are NOT captured. Then perform actions, then call again with since to read them. Reads chrome.* events from a ring buffer (global, per-event, 500 events/key). Use since cursor for incremental reads; tabFilter to limit to a tab. Returns { events:[{ args, timestamp }], nextSince, truncated?, droppedCount? }. For user-initiated browser actions where you need to react while the action is pending, extension_subscribe is still appropriate.

event.description: chrome.* event path, e.g. 'tabs.onUpdated'. Listener is lazily registered on first read — events before this call are NOT captured.

since.description: Timestamp cursor (ms). Return only events with timestamp > since. Omit to return all buffered events.

limit.description: Max events to return. Default: 200, max: 500.

tabFilter.description: Keep only events whose first arg matches this tabId (e.g. chrome.tabs.* events).

clear.description: Clear matched entries from buffer after reading. Default: false.

tools.name: read_realtime
tools.description:
Read realtime streaming events (WebSocket frames + SSE events) tracked via CDP. Complements read_network: shares CDP requestId so you can pivot between request metadata and live frame/event flow. Tracking is always-on (no first-call activation). Storage: up to 50 connections per tab, 5000 events per connection (ring buffer), closed connections retained 5 min then evicted.

**Two modes (mutually exclusive):**
- **Bulk mode** (no requestId): lists active WS + SSE connections with metadata (state, lastEventAt, eventCountSinceLastRead) and a preview of the most recent 5 events each. Filter via `protocol` and `urlPattern`; `limit` caps connection count; `clear` drops closed connections after read.
- **Detail mode** (pass requestId): full event sequence for a single connection. Use `since` (ms timestamp cursor) for incremental tail-f style reads, `eventLimit` to cap per-call event count, `includeBinary:true` to include base64 of WS binary frames in `dataBase64`. Response is sliced by BODY_CHUNK_SOFT_CAP (~900KB) on event boundaries; returns `nextSince` cursor when more events remain.

**Error codes:** all prefixed `[read_realtime]`. PROTOCOL_MISMATCH when requestId kind disagrees with protocol filter. CONNECTION_NOT_FOUND / CONNECTION_EVICTED for stale or closed connections. MUTEX_BULK_PARAMS / MUTEX_INCLUDE_BINARY / MUTEX_SINCE when bulk-only and detail-only params are mixed.

tabId.description: Tab ID. Get available IDs from tabs_context.

protocol.description: Filter by protocol. Default: 'all'. Use 'websocket' for WS frames only, 'sse' for SSE events only.

urlPattern.description: URL substring filter (bulk mode only; mutually exclusive with requestId).

limit.description: Max connections to return in bulk mode. Default: 100, max 500. (bulk mode only)

clear.description: Clear ALL closed connections from buffer after read (NOT filtered by urlPattern). Active connections preserved. Default: false. (bulk mode only)

requestId.description: Target a single connection by CDP requestId for detail mode. Mutually exclusive with urlPattern/limit/clear.

since.description: Timestamp (ms) cursor for incremental detail read. Use nextSince from previous response. (detail mode only)

eventLimit.description: Max events per detail call. Default: 100, max 5000. (detail mode only)

includeBinary.description: Include base64 of binary WS frames in dataBase64 field. Default: false. (detail mode only)
